papers.key_finding: Composition fluctuations satisfy a large-deviation principle whose quasipotential solves a contact Hamilton-Jacobi equation, and covariances of accumulated observables decay with accumulated volume rather than physical time.
papers.title: Large-deviations theory for growing chemical reaction networks
papers.tldr: The authors develop a large-deviation theory for exponentially growing stochastic chemical reaction networks by decomposing abundance into volume and composition, showing composition fluctuations obey a large-deviation principle with speed equal to system volume.
papers.why_relevant: It directly addresses stochasticity in growing biochemical reaction networks, connecting to Fangzhou's interests in microbial growth laws, cell-size homeostasis, and biomolecular reaction networks as a null model for single-cell heterogeneity.

papers.key_finding: Former-ICU drains harbor a highly conserved multi-kingdom core that remains resilient to structural changes and inactivity, with multidrug-resistant pathogens deeply embedded in integrated ecological networks.
papers.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and stability of multi-kingdom microbial communities in hospital sinks acting as persistent pathogen reservoirs
papers.tldr: A 17-month multi-kingdom study of 14 hospital sink drains combined 16S/ITS/18S profiling, culturomics, and resistance testing to track community assembly and stability through renovation and clinical use.
papers.why_relevant: It ties to Fangzhou's microbial population dynamics and community ecology interests by showing how environmental structure and anthropogenic shifts shape persistent, sink-specific multi-kingdom communities.

papers.key_finding: Taxonomic biodiversity plays only a minor role in maintaining stability during composting, thermophilic fungi cannot be replaced by bacteria, and keystone taxa and interaction networks not detected by abundance-based profiling promote process efficiency.
papers.title: Microbial Communities in Composting Processes:Succession, Functional Ecology, and Biotechnological Applications
papers.tldr: A review of composting microbiology spanning 2021-2026 uses genome-resolved metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and ecological network analysis to examine microbial succession, functional ecology, and biotechnological applications.
papers.why_relevant: It connects to Fangzhou's microbial community ecology and population dynamics interests, particularly the roles of keystone taxa, functional redundancy, and antibiotic resistance gene dynamics in managed microbial systems.

papers.key_finding: Circuit architectures were developed that produce distinct fluorescence outputs in primary, secondary, and tertiary roots by counting long-duration input pulses over the roughly two-day root branch specification period.
papers.title: Synthetic genetic circuits that count developmental cues in plant roots
papers.tldr: The authors built synthetic genetic circuits in Arabidopsis thaliana that use root primordium-specific promoters to express large serine recombinases, irreversibly inverting DNA segments each time a new lateral root initiates to count developmental cues.
papers.why_relevant: It directly addresses Fangzhou's synthetic biology circuits interest by demonstrating how repeated developmental signals can be converted into heritable DNA states for branch-resolution engineering.

papers.key_finding: The RBPF with updated noise covariance balances parameter estimation accuracy, state estimation error, and innovation whiteness compared with fixed noise covariance choices.
papers.title: A Modified Rao-Blackwellised Particle Filter Based on Updated Process Noise Covariance for Chemical Reaction Networks
papers.tldr: The authors apply a modified Rao-Blackwellised particle filter with recursively updated process noise covariance, based on the chemical Langevin equation, to jointly estimate parameters and states in a reduced-order gene expression system.
papers.why_relevant: It connects to Fangzhou's biomolecular control and reaction network interests by providing an estimation framework for stochastic chemical reaction networks relevant to synthetic and natural biological systems.

papers.key_finding: The composite reduced microbial alpha diversity and total biomass, disrupted biofilm architecture, decreased Actinomyces and Lactobacillus, and enriched Haemophilus and Granulicatella, with predicted functional changes in carbohydrate and nucleotide metabolism.
papers.title: N-acyl-homoserine lactonase–nanosilver composite modulates the bacterial community of an in vitro enriched biofilm model of early childhood caries
papers.tldr: An N-acyl-homoserine lactonase-nanosilver composite was tested on in vitro enriched biofilms from children with early childhood caries, with effects assessed by 16S rRNA sequencing, SEM, and biomass assays.
papers.why_relevant: It relates to Fangzhou's microbial community ecology and quorum-sensing interests by showing how a quorum-quenching enzyme combined with nanosilver alters community composition and metabolic function in a biofilm model.

papers.key_finding: Most respiratory pathogens were detected more often in oral fluid than lung, while lung microbiota showed lowest diversity and dominance by Escherichia-Shigella and Actinobacillus, and Clostridium perfringens presence was associated with distinct gut community composition and predicted functions.
papers.title: Pathogen detection and microbial community characterization in clinically symptomatic pigs from commercial farms
papers.tldr: The study combined molecular pathogen diagnostics with 16S rRNA sequencing of lung, oral fluid, and fecal samples from clinically symptomatic pigs on South Korean commercial farms.
papers.why_relevant: It connects to Fangzhou's microbial population and community ecology interests by characterizing how pathogen presence associates with site-specific microbiota structure and predicted functional profiles in a production animal system.

papers.key_finding: Community structure was primarily shaped by inoculum source followed by incubation temperature, with distinct genus-KO associations such as Pseudoxanthomonas with K12686 and K10804 in one inoculum.
papers.title: Effects of Inoculum Source and Incubation Temperature on Bacterial Community Structure and Predicted Functional Potential Associated with Polylactic Acid (PLA) Degradation
papers.tldr: Two compost inocula were enriched with polylactic acid under mesophilic and thermophilic conditions for 100 days to assess bacterial community structure and predicted functional potential.
papers.why_relevant: It relates to Fangzhou's community ecology and dynamic metabolism interests by demonstrating how inoculum and temperature select taxa and predicted functions linked to ester-bond hydrolysis and lactic acid metabolism.
